supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Anthropic planned, then abandoned roughly $7B MatX acquisition
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports, citing people briefed on the matter, that Anthropic discussed buying MatX for roughly $7B, that the acquisition talks are no longer active, and that discussions evolved toward a possible partnership. Reuters also reports Anthropic is expanding an in-house silicon team and meeting multiple chip startups.

contradictingEvidence.title: Neither Anthropic nor MatX confirmed the acquisition talks
contradictingEvidence.note: Anthropic declined to comment on the MatX deal talks and MatX did not respond. Reuters could not determine why the acquisition talks ended, so the exact economics and strategic rationale remain unconfirmed.

falsifier: Downgrade the vertical-integration thesis if Anthropic publicly says it is not pursuing meaningful custom-silicon development, if its chip-startup discussions do not lead to partnerships/acquisitions or deployed silicon, or if multi-provider rented compute remains economically superior enough that in-house silicon does not improve cost, latency, supply security, or gross margins.
title: Anthropic tests—but does not commit to—vertical integration into custom AI silicon
summary: Reuters reports Anthropic considered a roughly $7B acquisition of chip startup MatX, abandoned the acquisition path, and shifted toward partnership discussions while continuing to evaluate multiple chip startups and expand an internal silicon team. The evidence supports a frontier-lab vertical-integration experiment, not a confirmed acquisition strategy.
delta: Upgrade custom silicon from a distant infrastructure option to an active strategic path for frontier model labs, but downgrade the assumption that full acquisition/vertical ownership is obviously economical. Preserve the state as REPORTED_STRATEGIC_EXPLORATION rather than CONFIRMED_TRANSACTION.
firstOrderImpacts: frontier labs may seek lower inference/training cost and stronger supply control through custom silicon
chip startups become strategic partnership/acquisition targets for model developers
NVIDIA dependence may be reduced at the margin but remains substantial in the near term
secondOrderImpacts: AI competition may increasingly span model quality, cloud contracts, custom silicon, power, and capital structure rather than model benchmarks alone
large model labs may use partnerships instead of acquisitions when hardware ownership does not justify integration cost or execution risk
Nexus should track build-versus-buy decisions as evidence about the real economics of AI infrastructure

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Frontier-lab custom-silicon moves that progress from exploration to deployed production will predict improved unit economics or supply resilience before those benefits are fully visible in reported margins.
alphaHunter.baseline: public model revenue/growth and aggregate GPU-capex announcements
alphaHunter.alternativeData: silicon-team hiring, chip-startup partnerships/acquisition talks, foundry/tapeout milestones, direct accelerator purchases, cloud mix, gross-margin trends and compute-cost disclosures
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: lead time and forecast improvement for future compute-cost intensity, gross margin and provider concentration versus the baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the custom-silicon alpha layer if these signals do not improve held-out forecasts of compute economics or if frontier labs continue to rely overwhelmingly on rented third-party accelerators without measurable penalty.
